document.title: The sxml command: design
document.p: This page is for developers of the sxml program. The user reference, with every command, its options and examples, is apps/sxml/README.md ().

section.title: Design rules
section.p: These rules are binding for every command (). Sources: Command Line Interface Guidelines (https://clig.dev), POSIX.1-2024 XBD 12.2 "Utility Syntax Guidelines", GNU coding standards "Command-Line Interfaces", NO_COLOR (https://no-color.org).

section.title: One intent, one action
section.p: Every invocation does exactly what its words say, and nothing else.

item.p: Each command is one verb doing one thing. sxml check never also prints the document. Two behaviours get two commands or an explicit flag, never a mode guessed from the input (file or expression, XML or JSON).
The command line fully determines behaviour. No configuration files. The environment changes presentation only (color, once there is any).

No hidden side effects. sxml writes a file only when the command line names it (see "Written files" below), refuses to replace an existing file unless --force is given, never deletes anything, and never touches the network: fn:doc, fn:unparsed-text and friends resolve local files only.
Standard input is read only when - is given as a file operand.
Nothing is advertised that is not implemented. A command or option enters the program's table with its working code; planned ones are listed only under "Planned commands" below.

No abbreviations, no auto-correction. --form is not --format (unlike GNU getopt_long); a typo gets a "did you mean" suggestion and exit code 2, never a guess. An unknown option with no close match among the command's own that another command has is named as theirs: sxml xpath: unknown option '--expression'; it is an option of 'sxml xquery'. Commands have no aliases except help/--help and version/--version, which the guidelines ask for.

No repeated single options. --format=json --format=text is a usage error, not "last one wins"; collecting options (--param) say "repeatable", and one that must be given at least once (--schema) says "required; repeatable".
sxml [-h | --help | --version] COMMAND [ARGUMENT...]. Options before the command belong to sxml; after it, to the command.
Long options: --name, --name=value, --name value. Short options: -q, combined -qv, -o FILE or -oFILE (POSIX guidelines 3, 5, 6). Every short option has a long form.

Options and operands may be mixed after the command (GNU argument permutation). -- ends options: everything after it is an operand. - alone is an operand meaning standard input. An argument that starts with - (such as -1) must follow -- to be an operand.
A value-taking option always consumes the next argument: --expression -1.
-h/--help works on every level and wins over everything else on the command line before --, including errors: sxml version --bogus --help shows help. sxml help COMMAND equals sxml COMMAND --help.
sxml with no arguments is a usage error (exit 2) that prints the usage line: a script that forgot the command must not succeed.

section.title: Written files
section.p: Decided in (packet ). Three options name files to write; nothing else writes one, except the EXPath File functions that --allow-file-access grants ().

item.p: --output=FILE (-o FILE) on xpath, xquery, transform and serialize: the result goes to FILE instead of standard output, byte for byte what standard output would get. - and the empty name are usage errors (standard output is the default).

--result-directory=DIR on transform, for xsl:result-document with an href: DIR's file URI is the base output URI (XSLT 4.0, 2.4.6), so relative hrefs resolve against it; a result document whose absolute URI is not a file below DIR (.., another directory, another scheme, an escaped /) is an error, exit 3. DIR must exist; directories below it are made as hrefs need. Without the option, each result document is evaluated, reported on standard error ("not written; give --result-directory") and dropped. --output alone does not write result documents next to FILE: two intents, two options.

--allow-put on xquery, for fn:put (XQUF 3.0, 6.1; ): the document goes to the local file its file: URI names, resolved against the static base URI (the working directory), serialized with fn:put's $params. Other schemes are an error, exit 3. Without the flag fn:put raises FOUP0002, as the library does for a host that stores nothing. --allow-file-access does not imply it: that flag grants the EXPath File functions, a different feature.

is written to a temporary file beside it and moved into place in one step (POSIX rename, or link when not replacing, so a file that appeared meanwhile is not overwritten; MoveFileEx on Windows), so no reader sees it half written;
is committed only when the whole command succeeds; on any error every temporary file is removed and no file changes;
replaces an existing file only with --force (exit 3 otherwise, checked before the work starts and again when committing). --force without one of these options is a usage error.

section.title: Collections
section.p: Decided in (packet cli-3). F&O 4.0 (17.1.3, 17.1.4) leaves what a collection URI names to the implementation; in sxml it names a local directory, read as fn:doc reads a file: no flag, no network.

item.p: A collection URI is a directory, relative to the static base URI (the working directory, or the stylesheet's or module's location), with optional parameters after ?, separated by ; or &: select=PATTERN (file names; * any characters, ? one; default *.xml), recurse=yes|no (subdirectories too; default no) and on-error=fail|ignore (default fail). Another parameter, a fragment, another scheme than file: or a path that is not a directory raise FODC0002 with the reason.

fn:uri-collection gives the xs:anyURI of every selected file, sorted by path relative to the directory (byte order, which is code point order); nothing is read. The URI is the directory's URI and the relative path, the form fn:doc maps back to the same file.

fn:collection gives the document node of each of those files, in the same order, parsed as XML as fn:doc parses a file (external entities through the same resolver). Their document URIs are those URIs, and fn:doc of one gives the same node, whichever is called first. A file that cannot be read or is not well-formed makes the collection unavailable (FODC0002, naming FILE:LINE:COLUMN), or with on-error=ignore is left out. A collection holds documents only: JSON, text and other files are reached through fn:uri-collection and fn:json-doc, fn:unparsed-text or fn:unparsed-binary, one intent each, never a format guessed from a file name.

The default collection (fn:collection(), fn:uri-collection(), XPath 4.0, 2.2.2) is the one --collection=DIR names on xpath, xquery and transform: DIR relative to the working directory, optionally followed by the parameters above (--collection='docs?recurse=yes'). A DIR that is not a directory exits 3, an unknown parameter is a usage error; without the option there is no default collection (FODC0002).
Symbolic links are followed; with recurse=yes a directory reached twice (a link back up) is listed once.
Listing needs the platform's file system (apps/sxml/platform_file_system.c); where it has none (Windows today, ), every collection raises FODC0002.

The person running a command bounds its time, not sxml. The commands set no bound on evaluation steps (their one processor configuration is in query_command.c): a query runs to its end, and a run that takes too long is stopped with Ctrl-C (SIGINT) like any other program. The library's default bound of 10^8 steps is for programs that embed sxml and the JavaScript package; the conformance drivers set their own. sxml_processor_limits has no value for "no bound" (0 means the default), so the command asks for the largest count ().
Input stays bounded. Entity expansion is bounded to 4 MiB in every command that parses XML; a limit that is exceeded exits 4.

A document keeps the line and column of its nodes when the program can ask for them (, ). xpath, xquery and transform take --locations=automatic|always|never, the processor's sxml_source_location_policy: automatic, the default, keeps them for the documents a program reads (--context-item, INPUT, fn:doc, fn:parse-xml, --collection) when it calls fn:location, can reach functions dynamically (fn:function-lookup, fn:load-xquery-module, fn:transform, xsl:evaluate) or imports a schema; they cost 32 bytes a node (+45 % peak memory on a large document). always keeps them for every program, never for none.

Compile first, then parse. xpath and xquery compile before they parse --context-item, as transform does before INPUT, so the program decides; a static error is reported before a context document that does not parse.

An error that names a node says where it is. When the value of a dynamic error ($err:value: the third argument of fn:error, an xsl:message's select) holds a node whose document kept its locations, a second line follows the error: books.xml:4:3: the node the error names. For a program that cannot ask for locations, --locations=always gives it.
Results go to standard output; diagnostics, warnings and usage errors to standard error. Help requested with --help or help goes to standard output (it is the result) and exits 0.
Usage errors: sxml version: unknown option '--fromat'; did you mean '--format'?, the usage line, Try 'sxml version --help'. Control bytes from arguments are shown as \xHH.

Commands whose output another program may parse offer --format=json (sxml's own reports) next to the default --format=text. The JSON shape is a stable interface: fields are only ever added. Query results are not reports: they are serialized with --method= (Serialization 4.0 methods).

Help texts: a one-line summary that starts with a verb, a description in short paragraphs ending with the command's exit status, and examples that work on the sample files of apps/sxml/README.md. That page and the help agree: a change to one is a change to the other.

No color, no pager, no progress output today. When color arrives it is off unless the stream is a terminal, off when NO_COLOR is set and not empty or TERM=dumb, and --color=auto|always|never overrides both.

section.title: Planned commands
section.p: None today. The options the commands share: --format=text|json (report format), --context-item=FILE (parse FILE, or stdin for -, as the context item), --param=NAME=VALUE (repeatable; binds external variable $NAME to xs:untypedAtomic(VALUE)), --method=adaptive|xml|xhtml|html|text|json|csv (serialization of results), --output=FILE and --force (write results to a file; replace it), --locations=automatic|always|never (source locations of input documents, ). --output, --force and result documents arrived with packet ().
The QT4 and XSLT 4.0 conformance drivers are not sxml commands but developer tools under tests/ built with the same framework ().

item.p: apps/cli_framework/: declarative command tables (cli_command.h), the argument parser (cli_arguments.h), help and usage errors (cli_help.h), "did you mean" (cli_suggestion.h), output streams and writers (cli_output.h), dispatch and exit codes (cli_run.h). It never prints or opens files: all I/O goes through sxml_cli_output_stream.

apps/sxml/: the program table with the program's description and examples (program.c), the command handlers (command_<name>.c), main.c, and the platform layer: platform_stdio.c (stdio and the working directory, for the URIs of relative file names), platform_file_system.c (EXPath File) and platform_file_writer.c (the file writer of --output, --result-directory and --allow-put). The query commands xpath, xquery and serialize share (and transform reuses) their processor, the local-file resolver, --param, --context-item, --locations, the --method choices, error reports and result writing through query_command.h. A new command is one command_<name>.c plus one table entry, imitating command_version.c. Files are read through the invocation's sxml_cli_file_reader (cli_command.h), which the platform layer implements over stdio (command_check.c uses it), and written through its sxml_cli_file_writer (begin, commit, abandon; query_command.h's sxml_query_run_begin_file and sxml_query_run_finish).

Tests, all in tests/cli/ (registered from apps/CMakeLists.txt, outside the tests/*_test.c glob): framework unit tests cli_*_test.c, and end-to-end golden tests (sxml_add_cli_test: arguments, exit code, expected/<name>.stdout and .stderr; SXML_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 rewrites; WORKSPACE runs in an empty directory and compares the files written with expected/<name>.files). They run in tests/cli/input/, which holds the input files. The help texts have golden files too (expected/*_help.stdout): a change to a help text updates its golden file and apps/sxml/README.md together, and the README's examples are re-run on a release build and their true output pasted.
